findings.title: The Zig hook runner never sends session_id, so the primary shipped path stays single-bubble
findings.evidence: hook_runner.zig:56 extracts and validates session_id and uses it for session titles (lines 61-67), but neither /bubble body format string includes the field. Driven end to end: two Claude Code sessions through the real runner -> {"slots":1,"sessions":[{"session":""}]}; the identical pair with session_id -> {"slots":3}. ~/.claude/settings.json wires PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop to $HOME/.petdex/bin/petdex-hook, which main.zig:2822 routes into this runner, so this is the path Claude Code actually takes on this machine.
findings.impact: Issue #657's acceptance criterion (two conversations -> two bubbles) does not hold for the default Claude Code install; the feature only works via the TS CLI path.
findings.verified_at_layer: user (real binary, real socket, real payloads)

findings.title: omp-extension.ts and opencode-plugin.js also omit session_id
findings.evidence: Both build a bubble body with text/title/busy/agent_source and no session_id. Same collapse as F1 for those agents. Lower severity than F1 only because these adapters may not expose a session id at all.
findings.impact: Multi-bubble silently unavailable for omp and opencode users.

issue_candidates.title: session_id longer than 64 bytes silently merges two conversations into one bubble
issue_candidates.evidence: The server truncates to [64]u8 and keys by the truncated prefix; two ids sharing a 64-char prefix land in one slot (verified over real HTTP: two distinct 67-char ids -> one bubble). Not reachable through petdex's own producers, since both bubble-runner.ts safeSessionId (/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$/) and hook_runner.zig safeSessionId (len > 64 -> null) reject longer ids. A third-party poster holding the token could hit it.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: Requires a non-petdex producer plus the local token; the shipped clients cannot reach it.

issue_candidates.title: A multibyte session_id is truncated mid-UTF-8 into an invalid-UTF-8 key
issue_candidates.evidence: 30 x 3-byte chars truncated at byte 64 yields an invalid UTF-8 key; stored and matched fine because the key only feeds mem.eql and never a render sink (mirrorBubble takes no session param). Harmless today.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: No observable defect; both shipped validators reject non-ASCII ids. Worth a note if the key ever becomes user-visible.

issue_candidates.title: A token-holding local process can evict live conversations by posting 8 synthetic session ids
issue_candidates.evidence: 12 distinct sessions posted in a row evict earlier ones by LRU (verified live). Bounded by the 30/s shared rate limit (measured 39 accepted / 21 limited in a 60-request burst).
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: Requires the 0600 update-token, i.e. an already-local-and-authorized actor; the eviction policy is the intended slice-1 design.

issue_candidates.title: dropBubble does not set bubbles_dirty, so a server-side shrink is never pushed to the consumer
issue_candidates.evidence: After dropBubble, takeBubbles returns null (verified). Benign today because the only dropBubble caller is expireBubbles, which has already removed the bubble from the model. A future server-side dropper would silently desync.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: No reachable defect in this slice; the comment at hook_server.zig:183-185 states the assumption deliberately.
